frozen_problem.title: Source-boundary repair and a quantitative resonance profile
frozen_problem.statement:
Problem 2.4 may be an analysis of domino shuffling, since the set of Aztec diamonds is naturally divided into "equivalence classes" of size 2n by the shuffling algorithm.

2.4 Resonance

Some researchers have recently been studying combinatorial actions that are not strictly speaking of finite order, or at least not uniformly finite as some size parameter n varies, but still exhibit some forms of periodicity. An important example is Wieland's gyration operation on Alternating Sign Matrices (ASMs). When n is small, the 2nth power of the gyration operation on n-by-n ASMs is the identity map, so that all orbits have size dividing 2n, but as n gets larger this ceases to be the case. Instead one finds orbits whose sizes are "mostly" multiple of 2n, or submultiples k(2 n)/m where m is a small divisor of 2n. This is a fairly squishy notion, for what do "mostly" and "small" mean? Without having answers to these questions, we have charged forward and dubbed this "resonance"; part of the challenge here is making a good definition of the phenomenon being studied.

theory.target: Determine the minimum number and number of minimum-defect cyclic labelings of an arbitrary finite self-map, and falsify the claim that an optimal labeling must be surjective when the domain is large enough.
definitions: X={0,...,n-1}, n>=0; T:X->X is total and may be nonbijective; N>=1.
A labeling f:X->Z/NZ has unit-edge defect D(f)=#{x:f(T(x))!=f(x)+1 mod N}.
d and M are the unconstrained minimum defect and number of minimizing labeled functions; E counts exact labelings.
d_sur and M_sur impose surjectivity separately; absent surjections give null and zero.
c is the number of directed cycles; b counts cycles whose length is not divisible by N; incoming trees point toward cycles.
The empty domain has one exact labeling and no surjection; no phase quotient is taken.
assumptions: X={0,...,n-1} is finite; n=0 allowed. T is any total self-map, not necessarily bijective.
N>=1 and labels are fixed elements of Z/NZ; distinct functions are counted without quotienting by phase.
Defect counts vertices x with f(T(x)) != f(x)+1 mod N; all edges have equal unit weight.
Unconstrained minimization does not impose surjectivity. A factor requires exact equivariance and surjectivity; approximate surjective labelings are distinguished.
Every nonempty functional-graph component has one directed cycle and incoming trees.
No ASM, rowmotion, PL or birational dynamics are constructed; no new resonance definition or parent solution claimed.
approaches_considered: Minimize equation failures and assume n>=N preserves surjectivity; the three-state star falsifies even equality of the two minima.
Use one obstruction per bad directed cycle, choose a break edge and phase, and extend incoming tree labels uniquely.
Exhaust all label assignments and test every equation and surjectivity without using a functional-graph formula.
falsification_targets: Surjectivity costs nothing once the domain has enough states.
Bijectivity is necessary for the exact cyclic-factor criterion.
Incoming trees create extra minimum-defect phase choices.

claims.statement: For n>=N, unconstrained minimum equation defect can always be attained by a surjective cyclic labeling.
claims.falsification_condition: T=[0,0,0],N=3 has unconstrained minimum 1 but surjective minimum 2; a contradictory exhaustive assignment would invalidate this certificate.

claims.statement: For any finite total self-map with c directed cycles, b of lengths not divisible by N, minimum defect is b and the minimizer count is N^c times the product of the bad cycle lengths. Ordinary universal derivation, not independently proved or kernel accepted.
claims.falsification_condition: A missing component, alternative tree extension at the minimum, or an exact labeling/count contradicting the formula.

claims.statement: For every nonempty finite total self-map, exact regular cyclic factors exist iff N divides every directed cycle length; bijectivity is unnecessary. There are N^c exact maps when feasible. The empty map is not surjective.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed cycle-closing congruence, missing tail constraint or nonempty exact map that omits a target color.

claims.statement: For n>=N>=2, the constant n-state map has surjective minimum N-1 and N*(n-1)!/(n-N+1)! minimizers, versus unconstrained minimum 1 and N minimizers.
claims.falsification_condition: A smaller surjective defect or a miscounted assignment in the distinct exceptional leaf-color argument.

claims.statement: Separate methods agree on 10531 finite-map/modulus systems, verified by 955958 main-census label assignments; 24 star controls and 28 minimum-defect certificates pass, while seven corruptions fail.
claims.falsification_condition: A differing canonical case stream, missing domain, invalid certificate or accepted corruption.
